title: OpenAI Agents SDK: Handoffs, Guardrails, Tracing

questions.question: What are the five primitives of the OpenAI Agents SDK?
options: Node, Edge, Reducer, Checkpointer, Subgraph
Plan, Worker, Solver, Evaluator, Reflector
Tool, Prompt, Model, Memory, Trace
Agent, Handoff, Guardrail, Session, Tracing
questions.explanation: The SDK ships these five primitives.

questions.question: How does the model see a handoff?
options: As a tool named transfer_to_<agent_name> that the model can call
As a custom HTTP endpoint the runtime posts the conversation body to
As a system message injected before the next model turn begins
As a special reserved token the tokenizer emits mid-stream
questions.explanation: Handoffs are exposed as tools with the transfer_to_<agent> name shape.

questions.question: Which three guardrail types does the SDK ship?
options: Pre, post, and inline guardrails
Input, output, and tool guardrails
Hard, soft, and best-effort guardrails
Static, dynamic, and federated guardrails
questions.explanation: Input (first agent), output (last agent), and tool (per function tool) guardrails.

questions.question: What is the difference between parallel and blocking guardrails?
options: Blocking guardrails run in a background worker pool; parallel guardrails run inline with the main model call
Parallel guardrails always cost strictly more money than blocking guardrails do, regardless of whether a tripwire ever fires
Parallel runs alongside the main LLM (lower latency, wastes tokens on trip); blocking runs first (no wasted tokens on trip)
Blocking guardrails only validate the output of the last agent; parallel guardrails validate every single agent's output
questions.explanation: Parallel optimizes latency at the cost of wasted tokens when tripped; blocking saves tokens but adds latency.

questions.question: How is tracing enabled in the SDK?
options: Off by default; each individual agent must opt in via a config flag
Only via OpenTelemetry collector, with no built-in span exporter
Only on the hosted dashboard; there is no way to disable it locally
On by default; OPENAI_AGENTS_DISABLE_TRACING=1 opts out of it
questions.explanation: Spans for LLM, tool, handoff, and guardrail emit by default; an env var disables them.

questions.question: What is handoff drift and how does the lesson recommend mitigating it?
options: Agent A hands off to B which hands back to A in a loop; add a hop counter
Tracing falls behind the run under span volume; reduce spans emitted
Sessions overflow their backend storage; archive the oldest ones first
Guardrails desync from the deployed model version; retrain the guardrail LLM
questions.explanation: A hop counter caps transfer chains before they loop indefinitely.
